q: The two acceleration vectors \vec{a}_c and \vec{a}_T are perpendicular to each other. (2024)
e: Centripetal acceleration is directed radially inward while tangential acceleration is along the tangent, making them perpendicular.

q: The tangential acceleration is present in non-uniform circular motion. (2024)
e: Tangential acceleration arises from a change in the magnitude of linear velocity (speed), which occurs in non-uniform circular motion.

q: In a uniform circular motion, the magnitude of the velocity remains constant, but the direction of the velocity continuously changes. (2024)
e: In uniform circular motion, speed is constant while the velocity vector continuously changes direction along the circular path.

q: In rotational motion, the object rotates about an axis. (2024)
e: Rotational motion is defined as the motion of a body turning about a fixed line called the axis of rotation.

q: In uniform circular motion, the angular speed of the object is constant. (2025)
e: Uniform circular motion implies motion with a constant rate of angular rotation.

q: The centripetal acceleration and linear velocity are perpendicular to each other at every point in the path. (2025)
e: Centripetal acceleration points toward the center of the circle, perpendicular to the tangent vector of linear velocity.

q: Every particle on the rigid body has the same angular speed. (2025)
e: All points on a rigid body rotate through the same angle in any given time interval.

q: If an object rotates with constant angular velocity, its acceleration is zero. (2025)
e: Even with constant angular velocity, an object moving in a circle still experiences centripetal acceleration due to changing direction.

q: When the angular velocity is increasing, the angular acceleration vector points in the same direction as the angular velocity. (2025)
e: When rotation speeds up, angular acceleration and angular velocity vectors share the same direction.

q: In uniform circular motion, the velocity of an object changes due to a continuous change in direction, even though its speed stays constant. (2025)
e: Velocity is a vector quantity, so any change in direction represents a change in velocity.

q: A rigid body is a body that does not deform or change shape. (2025)
e: A rigid body is defined as an ideal solid whose distance between any two given points remains constant.

q: Centripetal acceleration is present only in uniform circular motion. (2025)
e: Centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and non-uniform circular motion whenever an object moves in a curved path.

q: Angular velocity and angular acceleration are scalar quantities. (2025)
e: Angular velocity and angular acceleration are vector quantities with specific directions along the axis of rotation.

q: Centripetal acceleration is present in both uniform and nonuniform circular motion. (2025)
e: Any circular path requires a centripetal acceleration directed toward the center of curvature.

q: In uniform circular motion, it has both tangential acceleration and centripetal acceleration. (2025)
e: Uniform circular motion has zero tangential acceleration because linear speed is constant.

q: Angular velocity is the rate of rotation with respect to displacement. (2025)
e: Angular velocity is defined as the rate of change of angular displacement with respect to time.

q: In a circular motion, the object just moves in a circle. (2025)
e: Circular motion is defined as the movement of an object along the circumference of a circle.

q: The angular acceleration is equal to zero when there is no change in angular speed. (2025)
e: Angular acceleration depends on the change in angular velocity (vector), which involves both magnitude and direction of rotation.

q: The direction of earth's angular velocity vector is along the axis joining its poles. (2026)
e: Earth rotates about its geographic poles, so its angular velocity vector lies along the rotational polar axis.

q: Angular velocity is the rate of rotation with respect to time. (2026)
e: Precisely defined, angular velocity is the rate of change of angular displacement with respect to time.
